what: M3 stride segmentation, validated on the 11 SPENT MoVi PG1 subjects. Ground truth from the mocap 3D; the estimate path on 3 clips.

shipped_method.detector: hysteresis (Schmitt) trigger, band 0.25 of the 5-95 percentile amplitude; no period estimate, so a changing cadence cannot break it
shipped_method.why_not_heel_strike: H36M-17 has no foot or heel keypoint, so there is no ground-contact signal; the standard substitute (Zeni et al. 2008, maximum anterior ankle offset) needs the direction of travel, and that direction is not readable on this footage -- see rejected_candidate below

rejected_candidate.method: Zeni et al. 2008: heel strike = maximum anterior ankle offset from the pelvis
rejected_candidate.needs: the direction of travel across the image
rejected_candidate.direction_read_from: running's duty factor -- stance is the shorter half-cycle, because running has a flight phase
rejected_candidate.above_one_means: the max->min pairing spans more than a whole cycle, so the method is incoherent on that clip rather than merely ambiguous
rejected_candidate.why_it_fails: MoVi subjects traverse the capture volume and turn around inside the window, so anterior reverses mid-clip and the statistic collapses to ~0.5

diagnostic_only: all 11 subjects are spent; this establishes no held-out claim
aggregate_only: no per-subject MoVi value is written here, same standard as the scoping files

ground_truth.source: 120 Hz Qualisys mocap, sampled at the video frame times
ground_truth.consistency_check: left/right cycle counts, which need no ground truth: two legs necessarily take the same number of steps

bars_in_overstride_strides.note: each bar sits outside the measured spread above, so it rejects a mis-segmentation rather than normal stride variability. Duration CV is REPORTED, not gated: a runner who decelerates inside the clip has a high CV and nothing is wrong

knee_peak_spread.why_it_matters: if stride-to-stride spread were as large as between-subject spread, a stride average would be averaging noise

fallback: when Strides.ok is False the report shows per-frame traces only and no stride table; stride averaging is a convenience, never part of the error budget
